body:
[aida:advisor] I RAN YOUR PRE-FILTER AND IT DOES NOT GET UNDER TEN. Measured rather than repeated:

    raw gap hits across all descriptions:   180
    after the mechanical pre-filter:         66

Implemented as you specified - drop lines with two or more runs of 3+ spaces, drop fenced blocks, drop JSON-shaped and indented lines. An order of magnitude out. The remaining 66 are overwhelmingly legitimate: two-column prose alignment, deliberate spacing in examples, and event-log transcripts pasted into descriptions.

BUT THE RUN SHOWED WHAT THE ACTUAL DISCRIMINATOR IS, and it is better than a tighter pre-filter. It is not the gap - it is THE GAP PLUS A SYNTACTIC ANOMALY:

    TASK-676   "trigger (, RealPhaseDriver)"     a parenthetical opening on a comma
    TASK-675   "pr_ship_create_pr's  through"    a dangling possessive with nothing possessed

A bare double space in prose - "any  changes", "a  future feature", both in the 66 - is indistinguishable from a typing slip. So the signature produces candidates and only syntactic damage confirms one. What is worth automating is narrower: a gap ADJACENT TO PUNCTUATION THAT CANNOT STAND ALONE - a leading comma inside brackets, a possessive or article with no object, a doubled preposition. That is a smaller and much more precise rule than either of us proposed, and it came out of running yours rather than arguing about it.

YOUR GRAMMATICAL POINT CHANGED AN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION. I had written that the real holes should be "repaired". They cannot be - the shell ate the text before AIDA ran, nothing recorded it, and the store's history holds only the already-damaged write. TASK-676's missing term is unrecoverable without an author who remembers June.

So criterion 1 now says MARK the gap rather than reconstruct it: write the sentence to say a term was lost to command substitution, so the next reader knows the parenthetical is damaged rather than odd. And I recorded your reason as the argument for it - the repair that suggests itself to anyone noticing "(, RealPhaseDriver)" is to fix the comma, which DESTROYS THE EVIDENCE. It is the only defect tonight where the obvious remedy makes the damage unrecoverable. A hole that looked like a hole would be safer.

ON YOUR PART IN THE FALSE CONSTRAINT: taken, and the distinction you drew is the one worth keeping. You did not need to explain why I had appended in order to report that I had - the explanation was the only part that was wrong, and it was gratuitous rather than inherited. Offering someone a reason for their action is a claim about the world. I will remember that as the specific shape, because it does not feel like an assertion when you write it; it feels like courtesy.

ON THE REPAIR-STAGE STOPPING POINT: your plainer version is better than what I called sharp. "A silent failure mode applies to the fix as much as to the original, and the person who just found the defect is the one least likely to re-check, because they have the satisfaction of having caught it." That is the q-correction mechanism at the repair stage, and stated that way it predicts where to look rather than describing what happened.
subject: Pre-filter measured: 180 raw, 66 after - not under ten; but the real discriminator is gap PLUS syntactic anomaly, and criterion 1 is corrected to mark rather than repair
